learning_paths.name: Deep Learning Fundamentals
learning_paths.why_this_order: Start with the breakthrough, then learn residual refinements and the broader practical course material.
learning_paths.expected_outcome: Understand data, architecture, optimization, and ablation discipline before touching multimodal models.
learning_paths.relevance_to_earnings_call_project: Keeps future visual/audio-sidecar work honest and benchmark-driven.

learning_paths.name: RNNs and Sequence Models
learning_paths.why_this_order: Move from intuition to memory mechanics, then regularization and ordering pitfalls.
learning_paths.expected_outcome: Design transcript sequence features with chronology, memory, and overfitting risk in view.
learning_paths.relevance_to_earnings_call_project: Supports section-aware prepared remarks/Q&A modeling and 30/100/500 transcript gates.

learning_paths.name: Attention and Transformers
learning_paths.why_this_order: Begin with alignment attention, then pointer-style extraction, then full self-attention.
learning_paths.expected_outcome: Understand why retrieval, evidence pointers, and rerankers should be citation-first.
learning_paths.relevance_to_earnings_call_project: Directly informs RAG, semantic retrieval, and evidence-span interfaces.

learning_paths.name: Scaling and Systems
learning_paths.why_this_order: Plan why to scale before studying how to scale.
learning_paths.expected_outcome: Separate data/evaluation scaling from expensive training infrastructure.
learning_paths.relevance_to_earnings_call_project: Defines when the project should move from deterministic baselines to local ML and later GPU experiments.

learning_paths.name: Multimodal AI
learning_paths.why_this_order: Learn practical vision basics, then landmark architectures and multi-scale context.
learning_paths.expected_outcome: Understand visual feature extraction as a measured sidecar, not a magic replacement.
learning_paths.relevance_to_earnings_call_project: Supports future video/status/prosody fusion only after transcript evaluation is stable.

learning_paths.name: Speech and Audio
learning_paths.why_this_order: Start with the applied ASR system, then revisit sequence memory and regularization.
learning_paths.expected_outcome: Treat ASR quality, acoustic coverage, and WER-style gates as prerequisites.
learning_paths.relevance_to_earnings_call_project: Frames audio as transcript provenance and later prosody evidence, not current production proof.

learning_paths.name: Complexity, MDL, and Compression
learning_paths.why_this_order: Move from applied model selection to neural simplicity, then theoretical complexity and dynamic complexity.
learning_paths.expected_outcome: Use compression and simplicity as evaluation guardrails, not as unsupported intelligence claims.
learning_paths.relevance_to_earnings_call_project: Guides boilerplate detection, weak-label governance, and model selection discipline.

learning_paths.name: Memory and Reasoning
learning_paths.why_this_order: Study external memory, relational memory, pairwise relation modules, then graph message passing.
learning_paths.expected_outcome: Design future conversation intelligence around explicit memory, speaker relations, and evidence graphs.
learning_paths.relevance_to_earnings_call_project: Supports Q&A relation graphs, topic-thread tracking, and analyst-management interaction features.

learning_paths.name: Signal Engine 2.0 Practical Roadmap
learning_paths.why_this_order: Start with evaluation humility, then retrieval/evidence, data scaling, audio provenance, and relation graphs.
learning_paths.expected_outcome: Convert research into staged, evidence-backed product architecture.
learning_paths.relevance_to_earnings_call_project: This is the shortest path from research layer to portfolio-grade Signal Engine 2.0 decisions.
